name: Gut-directed hypnotherapy (Manchester / North Carolina protocols; Regulora)
founders: Peter J. Whorwell, MD (gastroenterologist, University of Manchester / Wythenshawe Hospital)
Olafur S. Palsson, PsyD (clinical psychologist, UNC Chapel Hill; North Carolina scripted protocol, developed with UNC team incl. William E. Whitehead)
founded_year_range: 1984 (Whorwell, Prior & Faragher Lancet RCT). North Carolina scripted protocol ~1995 (Palsson & van Tilburg 2015: '20 years ago'; first trial report 2002). Regulora FDA 510(k) clearance K211463, 24 Nov 2021 (not De Novo).
cost_summary: Free at point of care in NHS units where commissioned. Private practice estimate: about GBP 80-150 or USD 120-250 per session (US upper bound sourced: Mindset Health 2023, up to USD 250/session; no authoritative UK fee data), so roughly USD 800-2,500 for a 6-12 session course. Regulora (prescription app, 12-week program) cash price about USD 942 (SingleCare, Oct 2026).
mechanisms: autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
mechanism_summary: IBS and related disorders are framed as disorders of gut-brain interaction, involving visceral hypersensitivity, altered motility and gut-focused anxiety or hypervigilance. Hypnotic suggestion and imagery are proposed to modulate visceral afferent processing from the top down. Evidence for this: rectal sensitivity normalised in Manchester data (Lea 2003), and anterior-insula responses to distension were attenuated in responders to both hypnosis and education, with posterior-insula attenuation specific to hypnosis responders (Lowen 2013). Hypnosis is also thought to reduce the gastrocolonic response (Simren 2004), somatization and distress (Palsson 2002), and catastrophizing (Gonsalkorale 2004). Immune effects are speculative, from UC work. The mechanism is not settled: UNC and paediatric studies found no change in rectal thresholds. The approach is organ-directed, with scripts tailored to colon, oesophagus or upper GI, and it makes no cross-syndrome claims.
techniques: gut-directed imagery (smooth-flowing river; hand on abdomen generating warmth)
suggestions of control over gut sensation and motility
North Carolina: 7 verbatim-scripted biweekly sessions over 12 weeks
Regulora: 12-week app-based self-hypnosis (7 x 30-min sessions, NC protocol) with breathing/relaxation
mainstream_notes: Recommended or suggested in NICE CG61 (2008; refractory IBS after 12 months), ACG 2021 (gut-directed psychotherapy for global IBS symptoms) and BSG 2021 (refractory IBS), and by Rome Foundation psychogastroenterology. Offered by NHS hospital units (Wythenshawe Manchester), Swedish nurse-delivered services, Dutch hospital programmes and US academic GI psychology services. Regulora (metaMe Health, built on Palsson's licensed North Carolina protocol) is FDA-cleared via 510(k) K211463 (24 Nov 2021).
insurance_notes: NHS-funded where commissioned (UK), and publicly funded in parts of Sweden and the Netherlands. In the US it is reimbursed when billed as health-behaviour or psychotherapy services by licensed clinicians; hypnosis-specific coding is often not covered. Regulora is a pharmacy-dispensed prescription digital therapeutic (cash ~USD 942); formulary coverage varies by plan and no Medicare or major-payer coverage policy was found.

key_trials.citation: Whorwell PJ, Prior A, Faragher EB. Lancet 1984;2(8414):1232-4
key_trials.design: RCT vs psychotherapy + placebo pill, severe refractory IBS
key_trials.finding: Hypnotherapy markedly improved all IBS features vs small gains in control; no relapse at 3 months

key_trials.design: RCT hypnotherapy vs supportive therapy + placebo vs medical treatment, functional dyspepsia (Manchester)

key_trials.finding: 71% initial responders; 81% of these maintained benefit up to 5+ years

key_trials.citation: Palsson OS et al. Dig Dis Sci 2002;47:2605-14
key_trials.design: Two uncontrolled mechanism studies of the North Carolina 7-session protocol
key_trials.finding: Large symptom improvement; no change in rectal thresholds/tone/autonomic measures; gains tracked reduced somatization and distress

key_trials.citation: Lindfors P et al. Am J Gastroenterol 2012;107:276-85
key_trials.design: Two RCTs in non-specialist settings (vs supportive therapy; vs waitlist)
key_trials.finding: Superior to supportive therapy in study 1; trend in study 2; effect lower outside expert centres

key_trials.citation: Moser G et al. Am J Gastroenterol 2013;108:602-9
key_trials.design: RCT: group hypnosis (10 sessions) + supportive talks and medical treatment vs supportive talks and medical treatment alone, refractory IBS
key_trials.finding: Post-treatment improvement 61% vs 41% (p=0.046); over 15 months 54% vs 25%

key_trials.citation: Peters SL et al. Aliment Pharmacol Ther 2016;44:447-59
key_trials.design: RCT hypnotherapy vs low-FODMAP diet vs combination
key_trials.finding: Equivalent GI improvement (~72%); hypnotherapy better for anxiety/depression; no additive effect

key_trials.citation: Lowen MB et al. Aliment Pharmacol Ther 2013;37:1184-97
key_trials.design: Controlled fMRI trial, hypnosis vs education (assignment; randomization not stated in abstract), women with IBS + healthy controls
key_trials.finding: Similar symptom relief both arms; responders showed insula attenuation to rectal distension, normalising toward controls

key_trials.citation: Rutten JMTM et al. JAMA Pediatr 2017;171:470-7
key_trials.design: Non-inferiority RCT home CD vs therapist hypnotherapy, children with IBS/FAP
key_trials.finding: Post-treatment success lower with CD (37% vs 50%); at 1 year 62% (CD) vs 71% (therapist), judged non-inferior

key_trials.citation: Flik CE et al. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2019;4:20-31 (IMAGINE)
key_trials.design: Multicentre RCT individual vs group hypnotherapy vs educational supportive therapy
key_trials.finding: Adequate relief at 3 months 41%/33% vs 17%; at 12 months 41%/50% vs 23%; group non-inferior (354 randomized, 342 ITT)

key_trials.design: RCT 6 vs 12 sessions (Manchester); no control arm

key_trials.citation: Lovdahl J et al. Aliment Pharmacol Ther 2022;55:1501-11
key_trials.design: RCT nurse-delivered individual vs group hypnotherapy

key_trials.citation: Berry SK et al. Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2023;21:3152-9 (Regulora)
key_trials.design: RCT digital gut-directed hypnotherapy app vs digital muscle relaxation, 12 weeks; co-author affiliated with MetaMe Health (378 randomized, 362 treated)
key_trials.finding: Primary pain-responder endpoint not met (30.4% vs 27.1%); secondary windows favoured GDH

key_trials.citation: Keefer L et al. Aliment Pharmacol Ther 2013;38:761-71
key_trials.design: RCT gut-directed hypnotherapy vs attention control, quiescent ulcerative colitis

key_trials.citation: Schaefert R et al. Psychosom Med 2014;76:389-98
key_trials.finding: Adequate relief RR 1.69, NNT 5; long-term NNT 3

key_trials.citation: Thakur ER et al. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2025;10:1075-88
key_trials.design: Network meta-analysis of behavioural therapies for IBS (67 RCTs)
key_trials.finding: Gut-directed hypnotherapy (12 RCTs) RR 0.79 vs waitlist; low/very-low certainty, publication bias

controversy: The criticisms are about evidence quality more than legitimacy. The 2007 Cochrane review found the trials too poor to conclude, and recent network meta-analyses rate certainty low or very low, with publication bias and no trials at low risk of bias. Much of the foundational evidence comes from the developers (Manchester, UNC) and from uncontrolled audits. Effects shrink outside expert centres, and hypnosis is not clearly better than relaxation or education in some trials; the Regulora pivotal trial missed its primary endpoint. Access is limited by the small number of trained therapists. Some patients resist the 'hypnosis' label, and adverse events are rare. A 2021 meta-analysis (Krouwel) found a non-significant pooled effect overall, with benefit only for higher-volume therapy; the paediatric home-CD format was less effective than a therapist immediately after treatment.

popularity.reach_estimate: ~10^5 (order 50k-200k) cumulative people. Basis: Manchester alone treated >1,000 patients by 2015 plus decades of NHS service; trials >3,000 participants; therapist-delivered services in UK, NL, SE, US; home audio/CD programs and Regulora. Excludes Nerva, which has its own entry.
popularity.method_notes: Social-media and Google Trends metrics were not quantified; there is no dedicated subreddit (discussion sits in r/IBS), and the Reddit API was blocked from this environment on 2026-10-13, so subscriber counts were not retrieved. The trajectory is anchored on documented milestones verified in PubMed and guideline records: 1984 first RCT; 2002 UNC protocol and Manchester service audit; 2003 long-term follow-up; 2008 NICE; 2012-2013 multinational RCTs; 2015 audit of 1,000 patients; 2019 IMAGINE trial; 2021 ACG/BSG guidelines and Regulora 510(k) clearance; 2023-2026 digital RCTs and four network meta-analyses. Levels are scaled relative to the program's own peak (2025-2026). The reach estimate is an order-of-magnitude extrapolation from audit sizes, trial enrolment and multi-country clinical services; Nerva app users are excluded. Reach estimate is a rough extrapolation, not a measured figure.
